title: Midyear proforma — surface tension modeling for pricing & HC
content:
Purpose:
This sheet synthesizes midyear budget revisions combining: 1) a refined headcount phasing for H2, 2) commitment vs on-demand GPU slab comparisons, and 3) a short pricing-elasticity sweep that shows where unit economics break/repair. The framing term we used in the meeting is 'surface tension' — how tight the unit margin is between committed capacity, pass-through pricing, and hiring cadence.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline: keep reserve commitments at current contract (30% of forecasted peak) and delay non-critical hires by 6–8 weeks. Projected burn reduction: ~6% by EOY vs previous plan.
- Low-demand shock (–20% tokens): need to cut 3 non-customer-facing ICs and suspend one staging GPU slab renewal to keep runway >14 months.
- Price compression scenario (–15% price): margin breakeven requires either 20% lower reserved GPU price (negotiate) or 15% hiring freeze plus temporary routing to lower-cost quantized variants.

Key assumptions (base-case):
- Revenue growth: 28% Y/Y for H2 2026.
- Token mix: 60% standard gen, 30% embeddings, 10% reranking.
- Average revenue per 1k tokens (base): $0.18 (weighted across routes).
- Reserved GPU profile: 8x A100-equivalent units across regions; committed discount vs on-demand: 36%.
- Fully loaded cost per SWE/ML eng: $280k/year (comp + burden).
- Ramp for new hires: 0% contribution first month, linear to 75% after 3 months, 100% after 6 months.

Levers we modeled (spreadsheet tabs referenced in linked sheet):
- HC_phasing: hiring by role, start date, ramp assumptions, comp bands.
- GPU_commit_vs_spot: month-by-month capacity plan with committed slab renewals and spot/ondemand fallback costs.
- Price_elasticity_scan: unit-margin sensitivity to price changes and token volume deltas.
- Catch-up_actions: operational levers (cache tuning, batching increases, quantization mix).

Representative tables (paste from the working sheet):
1) Headcount phasing (role, start, FTE, annual_cost) — CSV lines below for quick scan:
role, start_qtr, fte, annual_cost
SWE (serving-runtime), 2026-Q3, 2, 560000
ML Engineer (applied-ml), 2026-Q3, 1, 300000
Platform Eng, 2026-Q4, 1, 280000
SRE, 2026-Q3, 1, 200000
Product PM, 2026-Q4, 0.5, 90000
Total incremental annualized HC cost if hires executed: 1,430,000

Notes on HC: these are slotted against feature priorities: serving-runtime hires tied to throughput projects (batching/KV cache), ML hires tied to quantization/quality recovery. We intentionally front-load SRE & serving-runtime in Q3 because that directly reduces unit cost and can buy time vs pricing pressures.

2) GPU slab vs on-demand (monthly averaged snippet):
month, committed_hours_equiv, committed_monthly_cost, on_demand_estimated_cost, delta_pct
Jul-2026, 5760, 92,000, 138,000, -33%
Aug-2026, 5760, 92,000, 150,000, -38%
Sep-2026, 5760, 92,000, 125,000, -26%
(Committed shows consistent ~30–38% savings in base usage months; but if utilization dips <60% the savings evaporate)

3) Price elasticity quick-scan (unit margin / 1k tokens):
scenario, price_per_1k, tokens_rel_to_base, unit_margin_per_1k, net_monthly_margin_delta
Base, 0.18, 1.00, 0.07, 0
Price -10%, 0.162, 1.02, 0.048, -180k
Price -15%, 0.153, 1.04, 0.036, -340k
Volume -20%, 0.18, 0.80, 0.02, -420k
Combined (-15% price, -10% volume), 0.153, 0.90, -0.004, -950k

Interpretation: small price moves cascade because of fixed-cost nature (GPU and HC), and because customer-elasticity assumptions are modestly positive in our models (we assumed lower-priced offering wins some extra volume, but not enough to offset unit margin). The combined downside scenario breaches contribution margin and quickly eats runway without intervention.

Recommended action plan (short list):
- Negotiate a mid-year commitment reprice for the largest regional slab (EMEA 4x equivalent). Target: additional 8–12% reduction on renewal. Owner: Rahul. Deadline: 2026-07-20.
- Approve two Q3 hires (1 serving-runtime SWE, 1 SRE) now; hold back ML quantization hire pending a deeper A/B on quality cost tradeoffs. Owner: People Ops + Eng leads. Decision by 2026-07-10.
- Activate ‘catch-up’ engineering sprint: 4-week focused scope to squeeze 8–12% latency-to-cost improvements via batching and prefix cache eviction heuristics. Owner: Serving runtime lead. Start: 2026-07-05.
- Prepare customer-facing routing options (lower-cost quantized model variant) and a comms plan for limited fallbacks if price squeeze persists. Owner: Solutions Eng + Growth.

Open questions / risks (working notes):
- What is realistic reprice expectation from existing procurement partners? We used 8–12% as an internal goal but this is optimistic. If only 3–4% is achievable, contingency steps must be more aggressive.
- Hiring lag risk: if we miss Q3 start dates and demand rebounds, throughput constraints will cause lost revenue.
- Contract lock-in timing: one slab auto-renews in Sep with 60-day notice; missing the negotiation window adds substantial cost.

Quick audit trail / provenance:
- Numbers drawn from live usage export (linked sheets) and Q2 close revenue deck.
- HC comp bands validated by People Ops (Sophie).
- GPU rates taken from procurement quote log (Evan).

Next steps / asks from finance leadership:
1) Approve provisional headcount phasing shown above as conditional hires (two FTEs) so recruiting can start.
2) Greenlight negotiation mandate for slab reprice and a small DMV for ops to experiment with temporary slab suspension if utilization falls under 55%.
3) Review acceptability of the combined downside scenario and confirm runway threshold (recommended: 12–14 months).

TODOs (scratch):
- [ ] Plug final Q2 close numbers into sheet (Rahul) — blocking for final margin numbers. Due: 2026-07-06.
- [ ] Run sensitivity with alternate elasticity assumptions (elasticity = 0.6 and 1.2). Responsible: Finance modeling. Due: 2026-07-08.
- [ ] Draft procurement email template for reprice ask (Evan). Due: 2026-07-07.

Notes to self (informal):
- This model tries to bias near-term infra fixes because those are lower friction than permanent headcount cuts; also because infra wins compound over time (lower per-token cost multiplies over all usage).
- Keep comms tight — if customers see price movement we need to productize fallback routing fast.

Appendix (quick sensitivity outputs we should add to final slide pack):
- Tornado chart showing which lever moves runway most (reserve reprice, price per 1k, HC hiring delay, cache improvements).
- Waterfall showing monthly burn buildup under each scenario.
